correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the printed delayed system and uses only period integration, translation invariance of a periodic average, exact equilibrium identities, and two explicitly checked rational identities. Strictness is justified: zero weighted variance forces u constant; then the predator and prey equations force the whole solution to equal the coexistence equilibrium. The covariance identity follows by subtracting u_* times the log-prey balance from the undivided prey balance. The numerical specialization is exact rational arithmetic. No simulation or local Hopf approximation is used as proof.

originality.rationale: Statement-level comparison found no equivalent theorem coupling the delay-invariant prey mean, strict predator mean deficit and the exact lagged-covariance phase law for the Bai–Zhang delayed model. The source itself gives a period-integral identity only for its nondelayed planar system and treats the delayed system through spectral/Hopf calculations and simulations. Closest database records concern different oscillators or different predator–prey equations. The most closely related later additive-predation papers change the prey growth law or add predator self-competition, so their balance equations do not imply this identity.
residual_risks: Search is not exhaustive across all predator–prey literature; an equivalent balance law could appear under different terminology.

The 2024 and 2025 related papers were compared from accessible publisher material rather than every page of their full texts; they use materially different equations, so this is a limited residual originality risk rather than an unresolved decisive comparison.

An own-ledger theorem already uses a related rational mean-defect mechanism in another predator–prey ODE; the present finding is accepted only because the delay-specific covariance phase law is a distinct source-dependent constraint rather than a restatement of that mean defect.

value.rationale: The source’s central delayed phenomenon is repeated stability switching and Hopf-generated oscillatory coexistence. The accepted theorem supplies an all-amplitude constraint that those periodic coexistence states must obey: delay can change phase geometry but not the prey period mean, while predator mean loss is exactly tied to lagged phase covariance. This is more than a renamed Jensen inequality because the second identity connects a biologically interpretable yield deficit to the delay-specific autocovariance term. It is useful for checking numerical cycles and for interpreting how the density-feedback lag redistributes correlation without changing period means. A prior own-ledger mean-defect theorem on a different nondelayed predator–prey system was treated as a serious overlap check; the present result is not accepted for the mean defect alone, but for the exact delayed covariance/mean-loss coupling that has no counterpart in that prior item.
